wins: Captured detailed service/version fingerprints on exposed ports, establishing accurate situational awareness (ep001_step5).
Maintained persistence of attack flow by scripting automated banner grabs and logging the output for rapid verification (ep001_step7).
fails: Could not successfully transition from enumeration to exploitation, leaving attack without an executed payload (ep001_step14).
Repeated mentor interruptions indicate uncertainty in selecting exploitation vectors before privilege escalation (ep001_step11).
key_outcomes.summary: Run quickly gathered high-fidelity service data but stalled before exploitation; shift focus to translating enumeration into concrete attack paths.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Stalling between enumeration and exploitation due to indecision on next vector

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH port 22 is open and the banner indicates OpenSSH
skill_cards.then_action: Run SSH-specific nmap scripts to enumerate supported ciphers, users, and auth methods

skill_cards.if_condition: When multiple services present on adjacent ports
skill_cards.then_action: Use nmap service version scan with -sV and --version-all to correlate and prioritize potential exploit targets

skill_cards.if_condition: When strong service data collected but no exploitation plan exists
skill_cards.then_action: Correlate CVEs from version data, rank by exploitability score, and prepare tailored payloads (Metasploit or custom script)

memory_ops.reason: High fidelity service data consistently supports rapid enumeration and reduces blind exploitation time

next_experiments.title: Prioritized Exploit Planning
next_experiments.description: Take the captured service/version data, enumerate matching CVEs via searchsploit, and attempt exploitation starting with the highest likelihood target (e.g., known SSH/auth bypass or web service bug).

next_experiments.title: Automated Banner-driven Recon
next_experiments.description: Pipeline banner read to a script that triggers relevant nmap/auxiliary modules automatically to reduce delay between discovery and attack.
